{"candidate_slot":1,"current_prompt":"You are given a JSON input with two parts: 'system_profile' (a list of installed products with their versions) and 'advisories' (a list of CVE advisories, each with an 'id', 'description', and 'affected' field). Your task: determine which advisories affect software actually installed on the system, and return ONLY a JSON object {"applicable_cves":["CVE-..."]} listing the unique IDs of all applicable advisories (or an empty array if none).

Follow this procedure exactly:

1. PRODUCT MATCHING. For each advisory, identify the vendor/product from the 'affected' field (format vendor/product) and/or the description. Match it against installed products. Names may appear in the inventory in different formats: hyphenated (e.g., 'usta-aybs'), with underscores converted to spaces ('esp_hr_management' vs 'esp hr management'), with a package-manager prefix (e.g., 'netapp-snapcenter' for 'netapp/snapcenter'), or title-cased ('Gnome Libsoup' vs 'gnome/libsoup'). Treat these as the same product. Only match when the product is genuinely the same software; do not match superficially similar names.

2. VERSION COMPARISON. Parse versions as ordered lists of numeric segments, comparing segment by segment (e.g., 3.6.1.1 > 3.6.1; 2024.3.47707 < 2024.3.47707.1 is false — note inventory versions may have an extra trailing segment; compare segment-wise and, if one version runs out of segments, treat missing segments as 0 only when they are literally zero, otherwise a longer version with nonzero extra segments is GREATER than the shorter one). Compare numerically, never lexicographically (10.0 > 9.9; 20230607 is a single numeric segment).

3. BOUND SEMANTICS. The 'affected' field specifies version constraints:
- 'version < X': affected if installed version is strictly below X.
- 'version <= X': affected if installed version is less than or equal to X.
- 'version > X' or 'version >= X and < Y': apply the stated operators exactly; '>= Y' includes Y itself, '< Z' excludes Z itself. Installed version Y is NOT affected when the range is '>= A and < Y'; it IS affected when the range is '>= A and <= Y'.
- 'version = X': affected only if the installed version equals X exactly after numeric normalization (e.g., 2.6 matches 2.6.0 — trailing zero segments are equivalent).
- Multiple ranges joined by 'OR': the advisory applies if ANY single range matches.
- Phrases like 'versions prior to X are affected' mean version < X.

4. EDGE CASES.
- If an installed version equals a fix/boundary version mentioned with an exclusive operator, it is NOT affected (e.g., libsoup 3.6.1.1 installed, advisory 'version < 3.6.1' → not applicable because 3.6.1.1 > 3.6.1).
- If the installed version equals the inclusive upper bound, it IS affected (e.g., installed 19.2, advisory 'version <= 19.15' → applicable).
- Carefully check each segment: 4.10 > 4.9, so installed 4.10 is outside 'version >= 4.8 and <= 4.9'.
- A version slightly below the fix version IS affected (e.g., installed 3.7.1, advisory 'version >= 3.0.0 and < 3.7.2' → applicable).

5. DO NOT include advisories whose product is not installed, even if the description mentions other software. Do not infer applicability from description text alone; use it only to disambiguate product identity.

6. OUTPUT. Return only valid JSON: {"applicable_cves":[...]} with each applicable CVE ID exactly as supplied, no duplicates, sorted or in any order.
